title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
trick: Grade each agent run on two sheets, the deliverable and whether the native harness kept its trace-level obligations (delivered context, true exit codes, lifecycle), and the harness that wins one sheet loses the other.
framing_stripped: Called 'a mechanism-oriented benchmark that treats the native agent harness as the system under test' with 'evidence-based failure attribution'; it is a 4-harness x 9-model x 95-task grid with one selected run per cell, in which a second rubric (783 harness criteria, Appendix A.4) is graded by one LLM judge from normalized traces, and 'attribution' is a lookup of pre-declared (harness criterion, agent criterion) pairs that both failed, with the causal step ('validated propagation', $L_{\mathrm{val}}$) defined but never counted anywhere in the paper.
method_equations: One run is $R_{h,m,t,r} = (\tau, \Delta W, G, V_H, V_A, L_{\mathrm{act}})$ (eq. 2): $h$ harness, $m$ model, $t$ task, $r$ execution instance; $\tau$ the normalized event sequence, $\Delta W$ the workspace change against a frozen baseline, $G$ the apparatus-admission state (trace integrity, probes, oracle present), $V_H$ and $V_A$ the binary criterion verdict vectors of the Harness and Agent layers, $L_{\mathrm{act}}$ the set of activated candidate links. Per-run score (eq. 3): $$S = 50\,\frac{p_H}{n_H} + 50\,\frac{p_A}{n_A},$$ where $p_X$ and $n_X$ are the passed and finalized criteria of layer $X \in \{H, A\}$; items are unweighted within a layer; a combined pass is $S = 100$. Judge state 2 ('not exercised', Harness rubric only, Table 4) is resolved from the Agent outcome: pass if every Agent criterion passed, fail otherwise, so $V_H$ depends on $V_A$. An empty evidence selector scores 0 (sec. 3.4). Aggregates (eq. 8, 9): task success $M_A = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}_A|}\sum_{R} \mathbb{I}[Z_A(R) = \emptyset]$; $M_H^{\mathrm{micro}} = \sum_R p_H(R) / \sum_R n_H(R)$; $M_H^{\mathrm{macro}} = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}_H|}\sum_R p_H(R)/n_H(R)$, with $\mathcal{R}$ the reporting population (all 3,420 cells). Failure sets (eq. 4): $F_H = \mathrm{fail}(V_H)$, $Z_A = \mathrm{fail}(V_A)$, $Z_H = F_H \setminus B$ where $B \subseteq F_H$ are criteria made unobservable by an agent action (bypass); results use raw $F_H$ (sec. 4.3). A declared mechanism is $\ell = (h_\ell, a_\ell, \mu_\ell)$ (eq. 5): harness endpoint, agent endpoint, intervening distortion. Activation (eq. 6): $$L_{\mathrm{act}}(R) = \{\ell \in \mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{run}}_t \mid h_\ell \in F_H,\ a_\ell \in Z_A,\ q_\ell(R) = 1\},$$ with $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{run}}_t$ the task's candidate pool and $q_\ell(R) \in \{0, 1\}$ a pre-declared activation condition; $L_{\mathrm{val}} \subseteq L_{\mathrm{act}}$ requires manual review of event order and an observed intermediate distortion. Linked agent failures (eq. 7): $Z_{A,\mathrm{linked}} = \{a \in Z_A \mid \exists \ell \in L_{\mathrm{act}} : a_\ell = a\}$. Conditional link incidence per dimension $d$ (sec. 4.3): $100\,|L_d| / |J_d|$, where $J_d$ are runs with a failed criterion in both layers and $L_d \subseteq J_d$ those with a stored link; pooled over dimensions $842/1{,}700 = 49.5\%$ (Table 10). Grid (eq. 10): $4 \times 9 \times 95 \times 1 = 3{,}420$ cells.
load_bearing_assumption: That a Harness-layer zero measures the harness and not the adapter's view of it: harness criteria are judged from traces whose 'optional type-specific fields are populated only when the native source exposes them' (sec. 3.3.1), an empty selector is scored as a failure ('If a required selector returns no evidence, the current implementation assigns zero', sec. 3.4), and 'not exercised' criteria inherit the Agent verdict (Table 4), so the Harness macro ranking (Codex 59.8% lowest in every model group; OpenClaw 72.0%) is only a harness ranking if trace exposure, selector recall and mechanism reachability are equal across the four native observability interfaces (Codex JSON event stream, Claude Code stream-json plus session record, OpenClaw gateway JSONL, DeepSeek JSON-RPC notifications), which is never measured: 'The current analysis retains all finalized cells and does not estimate corpus-level selector recall, Judge agreement, or candidate-link precision' (sec. 3.6).
weakest_component: Single selected runs ranked by differences the paper cannot bound. Every cell is 'one selected execution' and 'The archive contains selected outcomes, including replacement executions from earlier recovery, rather than independent repetitions per cell. We therefore describe the observed matrix and do not estimate within-cell repeatability' (sec. 4.1); the headline harness effects on task success (Grok-4.6 33.7% OpenClaw to 55.8% Claude Code; Opus 5 30.5% Codex to 53.7% Claude Code, each over 95 tasks, Table 7, sec. 5.3) are therefore single-draw differences with a selection rule (rerun on recovery) that favours cells which failed first, no confidence interval, and 'Reasoning settings follow the archived configurations' (sec. 4.1), i.e. not matched across harnesses; the judge budget also differs by cell (4,096 tokens in 1,966 evaluations, 8,192 in 1,452, 32,000 in two, sec. 4.2). Second attack: the two layers are coupled by construction (state 2 'pass when all Agent criteria pass, and fail otherwise', Table 4; 'The two score sheets are distinct but not statistically independent', sec. 3.4), so the 1,700 'joint shortfall' runs and the 49.5% link-activation rate include runs where the harness mechanism was never reached and the zero is inherited from the agent failure. Third: the attribution module's causal claim is defined ($L_{\mathrm{val}}$) but no count of validated links, no judge agreement and no link precision appears in the paper; five hand-picked paired trajectories (Appendix F) 'support inspection of specific behaviors rather than a population-level estimate of attribution accuracy' (sec. 5.7).
regime: 4 native harnesses (Claude Code 2.1.220 and Codex 0.145.0 through a loopback LiteLLM gateway, OpenClaw 2026.6.9 native gateway, DeepSeek Harness 0.1.0-rc.6 JSON-RPC; Appendix B.1) x 9 model groups (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Gemini 3.7 Flash, GLM-5.3, GPT-5.6-Sol, Grok-4.6, HY3, Kimi K3, Opus 5, Qwen3.8-Max) x 95 tasks (15 Context, 27 Execution, 9 Governance, 19 Lifecycle, 7 Observability, 17 Tools, 1 Verification; 46 single-turn, 45 fixed multi-turn, 4 simulator-driven; 59 workflow, 22 terminal, 14 coding), one selected run per cell = 3,420 runs in Docker; wall-time ceilings 120-5,400 s, 1-120 user turns, 5-300 task-tool calls (ceilings, not observed counts, sec. 4.2); judge deepseek-v4-flash for all cells. Outcomes: Agent Pass (all Agent criteria) 35.8% Codex to 44.0% Claude Code; Harness macro 59.8% Codex to 72.0% OpenClaw; Clean (both layers) 286/3,420 = 8.4%; 1,065/3,420 = 31.1% Agent success with a failed Harness criterion; joint shortfall 1,700, of which 842 (49.5%) carry a stored candidate link; 1,773 of 2,069 Agent-failure runs (85.7%) keep an unlinked failed criterion (Table 10, sec. 5.5). Mean recorded tokens per run 372.7k (DeepSeek Harness) to 680.0k (OpenClaw); mean estimated agent cost $0.436 (Claude Code) to $0.633 (OpenClaw), judge cost excluded (sec. 5.6). 783 Harness and 556 Agent criteria: 909 programmatic rules, 430 semantic rubrics (Appendix A.4).
information_asymmetry: (1) Per-cell vs repeated: the quantity CL-W43-14 needs, the within-cell run-to-run spread against which a 12.2-point harness-macro range and 22-23-point task-success swings are to be judged, is absent by design ('does not estimate within-cell repeatability', sec. 4.1) while the released archive holds the discarded 'replacement executions from earlier recovery' for some cells, i.e. a partial second draw exists on disk but is excluded from every table; the paper settles that the two rankings disagree and leaves open whether either ranking is stable, and it is itself an instance of the claim's target (a single-run leaderboard with replacement selection). (2) Effort vs harness: the per-run token_usage event records reasoning tokens and the resolved configuration records the reasoning setting per cell (sec. 4.1, Appendix C.3), so the dose-matched comparison CL-W43-03 asks for (does Claude Code's +23.2 points on Opus 5 survive matching reasoning tokens and counting restarts) is computable from the release but not run; the paper settles nothing for CL-W43-03 and supplies the first public grid where effort, restarts and harness identity are all logged per cell. (3) Delivered vs used: the tracer's model_input and tool_result events establish 'what the model could observe' (sec. 2.3, 3.1), the exact dose-delivered record that CL-W43-10 lacks, and the Context dimension scores whether information survived a boundary (cross-turn fact retention: 48.4% Harness satisfaction with 95.8% Agent success; subagent result aggregation: 46.2% vs 72.2% over 144 runs, sec. 5.4), which says the agent succeeded without the delivered content in half the runs; but no content is ever varied, so presence-vs-content stays open while the instrument to test it (per-run model-facing context plus authoritative state) is now published. (4) Co-occurrence vs propagation: the run knows event order, intermediate distortion and the agent's next action (Table 34), but the reported statistic is the fraction of joint failures with a declared pair (49.5%); the validated set is never counted, so harness-caused vs agent-caused remains a label, not a measurement. (5) Harness obligation vs trace exposure: whether a harness zero is a harness defect or an adapter blind spot (empty selector = 0) is decidable from the admission and selector-coverage records that are kept 'separate from performance aggregates' (sec. 3.6) and never crossed with the scores.
occupies: A published 4-harness x 9-model x 95-task grid (3,420 runs, traces, verdicts released) with a seven-component harness-obligation taxonomy and a two-sheet score, showing that the harness leading on all-criteria task success (Claude Code, 44.0%) is not the one leading on harness-criterion satisfaction (OpenClaw, 72.0% macro), that 1,065 of 3,420 runs (31.1%) succeed with at least one failed harness criterion, that 842 of 1,700 joint-failure runs (49.5%) match a pre-declared harness-to-agent mechanism pair, and a trace intermediate representation with per-boundary evidence authority; for CL-W43-03 it occupies the observation that harness identity moves single-run task success by up to 23.2 points at fixed model (not its decomposition into effort or restarts); for CL-W43-14 it is a new instance of the unreplicated leaderboard, not an answer; for CL-W43-10 it occupies 'context delivered but outcome unchanged' as a harness-fidelity finding, not a content-vs-presence test.

neighbors.title: Harness-Bench: Evaluating Agent Harnesses across Models and Realistic Workflows
neighbors.trick: Run several native harnesses on 106 sandboxed tasks across model backends under shared budgets and record traces, usage and validator output per run (5,194 trajectories), concluding capability should be reported per model-harness pair; this card's paper adds a second, harness-obligation score sheet on top of the same design.

neighbors.title: Auditing Agent Harness Safety
neighbors.trick: Audit the whole trajectory of 210 tasks for boundary compliance, execution fidelity and stability across ten harness configurations, finding a correct final answer can sit on an unauthorized access or a context leak mid-run; the same 'outcome hides the violation' move, aimed at safety rather than reliability.

neighbors.title: AgentRx: Diagnosing AI Agent Failures from Execution Trajectories
neighbors.trick: Annotate 170 failed trajectories with a critical failure step and category, then have an LLM synthesize and check constraints step by step so a judge can localize the step (75% better localization than prior work); step-level blame on the agent, where this card's paper blames a harness obligation.

neighbors.title: REFLECT: Intervention-Supported Error Attribution for Silent Failures in LLM Agent Traces
neighbors.trick: Guess the error step, patch it and replay the trace, and use whether the outcome flips as evidence to refine the attribution; the interventional check that this card's paper's 'validated propagation' set describes but never runs.

neighbors.title: Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When? On Automated Failure Attribution of LLM Multi-Agent Systems
neighbors.trick: Collect failure logs from 127 multi-agent systems with the responsible agent and decisive step annotated, and show the best automatic method finds the agent 53.5% of the time and the step 14.2%; the prior that pre-declared mechanism pairs cannot be trusted without a precision number.

theme_fit.why: scaffold sensitivity at fixed model (up to 23.2 points), a second instrument for harness fidelity, attribution of outcome to harness vs agent, and a single-run leaderboard with no replication: the lane's attribution and reliability questions, with the data released

the Context and Lifecycle dimensions score whether facts survive turn boundaries, compaction and subagent returns (cross-turn retention 48.4% harness vs 95.8% agent; subagent aggregation 46.2% vs 72.2%), a measured handoff cost, but content is never varied

per-harness token and dollar accounting with cache-read partitioning at frozen prices (Opus 5: $0.660 on Claude Code at 383.1k mean tokens vs $2.121 on Codex at 490.4k, Table 7, a 3.2x cost gap on 1.3x tokens), reported, not modeled; 'does not interpret duration differences as a controlled throughput experiment'

limitations_as_complaints: I ran one selected execution per harness-model-task cell, some of them replacement runs after recovery, so I cannot say whether my 12.2-point harness-macro range or the 23.2-point swing in Opus 5's task success across harnesses would survive a second draw: 'The archive contains selected outcomes, including replacement executions from earlier recovery, rather than independent repetitions per cell. We therefore describe the observed matrix and do not estimate within-cell repeatability' (sec. 4.1; sec. 6.1: 'limited evidence about generalization to deployment workloads or stability across repeated runs').

My harness comparison is not dose-matched: reasoning settings 'follow the archived configurations', judge budgets differ by cell, and task revisions and recovery runs differ, so I cannot attribute a difference between harnesses to a harness design choice: 'Variation in task revisions, runtime settings, and scoring budgets further constrains causal conclusions about individual harness design choices' (sec. 6.1; sec. 4.2: 'Task-specific revisions and recovery runs also limit causal interpretations of a difference between Harnesses').

My failure attribution stops at co-occurrence: a 'harness_caused' label means a pre-declared pair both failed, I never count validated propagations, I never measure judge agreement or link precision, and an empty evidence selector is scored as a harness failure: 'The current analysis retains all finalized cells and does not estimate corpus-level selector recall, Judge agreement, or candidate-link precision' (sec. 3.6; sec. 5.5: 'Fewer than half of jointly failing runs contain a stored link, and most Agent-failure runs retain at least one failed criterion not reached by any link').
